Naruhito (born 23 February 1960) is Emperor of Japan.

Benjamin Netanyahu (born 21 October 1949), nicknamed "Bibi", is an Israeli politician and diplomat who has served as Prime Minister of Israel since 2022.

Mary I: Mary was the only surviving child of Henry VIII by his first wife, Catherine of Aragon.

Alexander I of Russia: The eldest son of Paul I of Russia and Sophie Dorothea of Württemberg, Alexander succeeded to the throne after his father was murdered.

Vlad the Impaler: Vlad and his younger brother, Radu, were held as hostages in the Ottoman Empire in 1442 to secure their father's loyalty.

Queen Victoria: Victoria was the daughter of Prince Edward, Duke of Kent and Strathearn (the fourth son of King George III), and Princess Victoria of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld.

2023 Lewiston shootings: United States. On October 25, 2023, 40-year-old Robert Card carried out a spree shooting in Lewiston, Maine, United States, killing 18 people and wounding 13 others.

Yabloko: Russia. The party consequently participated in the elections of deputies of the State Duma of the Federal Assembly of the Russian Federation of all eight convocations.
In which country was Dominion of India?
Dominion of India: United Kingdom. Until its independence, India had been ruled as an informal empire by the United Kingdom.
In which country did the Battle of Stamford Bridge take place?
Battle of Stamford Bridge: Kingdom of England. After a bloody battle, both Hardrada and Tostig, along with most of the Norwegians, were killed.
In which country did the Mukden incident take place?
Mukden incident: Republic of China. The Mukden incident was a false flag event staged by Japanese military personnel as a pretext for the 1931 Japanese invasion of Manchuria.
In which country is Operation Red Wings?
Operation Red Wings: Afghanistan. Consequently, Shah and his group were one of the primary targets of the American military operation.
In which country is Five Star Movement based?
Five Star Movement: Italy. The Five Star Movement (Italian: Movimento 5 Stelle [moviˈmento ˈtʃiŋkwe ˈstelle], M5S) is a political party in Italy, led by Giuseppe Conte.

Battle of Karbala: Iraq. Battle ensued on 10 October during which Husayn was killed along with most of his relatives and companions, while his surviving family members were taken prisoner.
In which country did the Battle of Red Cliffs take place?
Battle of Red Cliffs: People's Republic of China. The Battle of Red Cliffs, also known as the Battle of Chibi, was a decisive naval battle in China that took place during the winter of 208–209 AD.
Which of these is an official language of Shang dynasty?
Shang dynasty: Old Chinese. The classic account of the Shang comes from texts such as the Book of Documents, Bamboo Annals and Shiji.
Which of these was an official language of Almohad Caliphate?
Almohad Caliphate: Arabic. The Almohad Caliphate or Almohad Empire was a North African empire ruled by a Berber Muslim dynasty in the 12th and 13th centuries that lasted from 1121-1269.
Which of these was an official language of Assyria?
Assyria: Akkadian. The remaining Assyrian people, who have survived in northern Mesopotamia to modern times, were gradually Christianized from the 1st century AD onward.
Of which country is Pataliputra the capital?
Pataliputra is the capital of Gupta Empire. The Gupta Empire was an Indian empire during the classical period of the Indian subcontinent which existed from the mid 3rd century to mid 6th century CE.
This Iraqi militant became the second caliph of the Islamic State in 2019, appointed by a shura council within a week of his predecessor's suicide, and died by his own suicide in 2022. Who was he?

Abu Ibrahim al-Hashimi al-Qurashi (born Amir Mohammed Abdul Rahman al-Mawli al-Salbi; 1 or 5 October 1976 - 3 February 2022) was an Iraqi militant and the second caliph of the Islamic State from 2019 until his suicide in 2022.
Nicknamed 'the Blessed,' he took the Russian throne after his father's murder and steered the empire through the chaos of the Napoleonic Wars. Who was he?
Alexander I of Russia was Emperor of Russia (1801–1825).

Before he ever entered Parliament, this Welshman was a miners' union firebrand in the 1926 general strike — but he's best remembered for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service as Attlee's Minister of Health. Who was he?

Aneurin Bevan (15 November 1897 - 6 July 1960) was a Welsh Labour Party politician, noted for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service during his tenure as Minister of Health in Clement Attlee's government.

This Burmese politician and diplomat served as State Counsellor from 2016 to 2021 and was instrumental in Myanmar's transition from military rule toward democracy. She's been the general secretary of the National League for Democracy since the party's founding in 1988 — who is she?
Aung San Suu Kyi (born 19 June 1945) is a Burmese politician, diplomat and author who served as State Counsellor of Myanmar and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2016 to 2021.

The longest-serving independent in U.S. congressional history, this Vermont senator and self-described democratic socialist sought the Democratic presidential nomination in both 2016 and 2020 — who is he?
Bernie Sanders (born September 8, 1941) is an American politician and activist serving as the senior United States senator from Vermont, a seat he has held since 2007.
This Finnish military commander led the Whites during his country's 1918 civil war, later commanded its armed forces through WWII, and became president from 1944 to 1946 — who is he?
Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim (Finland) was a Finnish military commander and statesman.

Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire

Cisplatine War was an armed conflict fought in the 1820s between the Empire of Brazil and the United Provinces of the Ro de la Plata over control of the Banda Oriental following its annexation by Brazil as the Cisplatina province.
Before running for president and serving in Congress, this Minnesota politician co-owned a gelato brand, a vodka brand, and a Twin Cities coffeehouse chain. Who is he?
Dean Phillips (n Pfefer; born January 20, 1969) is an American politician, businessman, and former presidential candidate who served from 2019 to 2025 as the U.S.
Serving as deputy to Erich Honecker from 1984 before taking over the top job in 1989, this East German leader was forced out within weeks as the Wall came down — who is he?
Egon Krenz (German; born 19 March 1937) is a German former politician who was the last Communist leader of the German Democratic Republic (East Germany) during the Revolutions of 1989.
This former guerrilla movement, born from a 1980 merger of leftist Salvadoran factions, later became a political party after El Salvador's long civil war ended in 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front is a Salvadoran left-wing political party and former guerrilla rebel group.
Nicknamed for a Washington State river where his first victims were found, this American was convicted of 49 murders committed between 1982 and 1998 — who is he?

Gary Ridgway (born February 18, 1949), known as the Green River Killer or the Green River Strangler, is an American serial killer who was convicted of murdering forty-nine women between 1982 and 1998 in the northwestern United States.

The first Democrat elected president after the Civil War, this former Buffalo mayor and New York governor holds a unique distinction: he's the only president to serve two nonconsecutive terms. Who was he?
Grover Cleveland (March 18, 1837 - June 24, 1908) was the 22nd and 24th president of the United States, serving from 1885 to 1889 and from 1893 to 1897.

Taught to fly by the Wright brothers themselves, this aviation pioneer became the only American to hold five-star rank in two different branches of the military and founded what became the RAND Corporation — who was he?
Henry H. Arnold (25 June 1886 - 15 January 1950) was an American general officer holding the ranks of General of the Army and later, General of the Air Force.
Son of a former prime minister, this Cambodian leader rose through the Royal Cambodian Army to deputy commander-in-chief before taking his father's job in 2023 — who is he?

Hun Manet (born 20 October 1977) is a Cambodian politician and military officer who has served as Prime Minister of Cambodia and Vice President of the ruling Cambodian People's Party (CPP) since 2023.

A prominent Brexit-supporting Conservative MP, this British politician chaired the eurosceptic European Research Group before serving as Leader of the House of Commons and, briefly, as business secretary. Who is he?
Jacob Rees-Mogg (born 24 May 1969) is a British politician, businessman and broadcaster who served as the member of Parliament (MP) for North East Somerset from 2010 to 2024.
Before becoming U.S. secretary of defense in 2017, this Marine Corps four-star general led both U.S. Central Command and NATO's Supreme Allied Command Transformation — who is he?
Jim Mattis (born September 8, 1950) is an American military officer who served as the 26th United States secretary of defense from 2017 to 2019.

This South African politician founded and leads a communist, black nationalist party, having previously served as president of the African National Congress's Youth League before his expulsion from the party in 2012 — who is he?
Julius Malema (born 3 March 1981) is a South African politician.

Beginning in 1881 with the crowning of a Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen prince as King Carol I and ending with King Michael I's 1947 abdication, this constitutional monarchy grew from an earlier union of Moldavia and Wallachia — which kingdom?
Kingdom of Romania was a constitutional monarchy that existed from 1881 to 1947.
Championing free speech, free assembly, market economies and the rule of law, this political philosophy centers on the rights of the individual — what is it?
Liberalism is a political and moral philosophy based on the rights of the individual, liberty, consent of the governed, political equality, right to private property, and equality before the law.
This Panamanian military officer ruled his country through puppet presidents in the 1980s, amassing a fortune from drug trafficking despite long ties to American intelligence — who was he?
Manuel Noriega (mahn-WEL; February 11, 1934 - May 29, 2017) was a Panamanian military officer and politician who was the de facto ruler of Panama from 1983 to 1989.

A former physician, this Azerbaijani politician serves as both First Lady and First Vice President of her country — a position her husband, the president, created in 2017 specifically to appoint her to it. Who is she?
Mehriban Aliyeva (ne Pashayeva; born 26 August 1964) is an Azerbaijani politician and former physician who is the First Vice President and First Lady of Azerbaijan.
Succeeding his late brother in 2006, this Emirati royal serves as UAE vice president and prime minister while ruling the emirate behind the Burj Al Arab — who is he?
Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum (born 15 July 1949) is an Emirati politician and royal who is the current ruler of Dubai, and serves as the vice president and prime minister of the UAE.

Formed in 1961 through a merger between a farmer-labor movement and the country's Labour Congress, this left-leaning Canadian federal political organization has served as Official Opposition but never won enough seats to form government — which one?
New Democratic Party (NDP) is a federal political party in Canada.

Serving two non-consecutive terms as Kerala's chief minister and representing the same constituency from 1970 until his death in 2023, this Indian statesman was honored by the United Nations for public service in 2013 — who was he?
Oommen Chandy (31 October 1943 - 18 July 2023) was an Indian lawyer and statesman who served as the tenth chief minister of Kerala, serving from 2004 to 2006 and 2011 to 2016.

Serving as the Shinawatra family's main political vehicle since its founding as the third incarnation of a party ex-PM Thaksin Shinawatra started in 1998, this party has led Thailand's ruling coalition since 2023 — which party?
Pheu Thai Party (PTP or PT; lit. 'For Thais Party') is a major populist, liberal conservative political party in Thailand.
Born in 1988, this Indian politician served as an MLA from Delhi's Rajinder Nagar before joining the Rajya Sabha in 2022 and later switching parties to the BJP — who is he?
Raghav Chadha (born 11 November 1988) is an Indian politician and chartered accountant who serves as a Member of Parliament in the Rajya Sabha since 2022.
This TV executive served as a media consultant to three Republican presidents before becoming chairman and CEO of Fox News — who is he?
Roger Ailes (May 15, 1940 - May 18, 2017) was an American television executive and media consultant.
Elected mayor of Wasilla, Alaska in 1996 before becoming the state's ninth governor a decade later, this politician was John McCain's running mate in the 2008 presidential race — who is she?
Princess Alice of the United Kingdom
Sarah Palin (ne Heath; born February 11, 1964) is an American politician, commentator, and author who served as the ninth governor of Alaska from 2006 until her resignation in 2009.

Founded in 1930 on the teachings of a 13th-century Buddhist priest and centered on chanting a phrase from the Lotus Sutra, this Japanese new religious movement has been led by Minoru Harada since 2023 — which organization?
Soka Gakkai ("creating value study group") is a Japanese new religion founded in 1930 based on the teachings of the 13th-century Japanese Buddhist priest Nichiren.
This shamanistic belief system of the Eurasian steppes centered on a sky god and served as the state religion of several medieval Turkic and Mongolic khaganates — what is it?
Tengrism (also known as Tengriism, Tengerism, or Tengrianism) is a belief system originating in the Eurasian steppes, based on shamanism and animism.

One of the few government agencies explicitly authorized by the U.S. Constitution, this independent federal agency began operations in 1971, replacing a former Cabinet department, and now employs over half a million career workers — name this agency?

United States Postal Service (USPS; also known as the Post Office, U.S. Mail, or simply the Postal Service) is an independent agency of the executive branch of the United States federal government responsible for providing postal service in the United States.

Sparked by Britain's restrictions on American trade and the Royal Navy's impressment of sailors, this conflict was fought during the wider Napoleonic Wars and dragged on even after the Treaty of Ghent was signed — what was it?
War of 1812 was a conflict initiated by the United States against the United Kingdom and its allies fought mainly in North America and at sea during the wider Napoleonic Wars.
A Hindu monk who became one of India's youngest MPs at 26, he has since 2017 been the longest-serving chief minister of Uttar Pradesh — who is he?
Yogi Adityanath (born Ajay Mohan Singh Bisht; 5 June 1972) is an Indian Hindu monk and politician.
Serving as Iraq's president from 2022 to 2026, he previously ran the country's Ministry of Water Resources and became just the fourth non-Arab to hold the top office — who is he?
Abdul Latif Rashid: President of Iraq from 2022 to 2026. Rashid was formerly a spokesperson for the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) in the United Kingdom.
A former judge who once led Turkey's Constitutional Court, this staunch secularist served as Turkish president from 2000 to 2007, succeeding Suleyman Demirel — who is he?
Ahmet Necdet Sezer: President of Turkey from 2000 to 2007. Ahmet Necdet Sezer (born 13 September 1941) is a Turkish statesman and judge who served as the president of Turkey from 2000 to 2007.
This Bolshevik revolutionary served as premier of both Russia and the Soviet Union in the 1920s before becoming one of the accused in Stalin's Great Purge show trials — who is he?
Alexei Rykov: Premier of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1930.
Dubbed "the Butcher of Rostov" and "the Red Ripper," this Soviet serial killer murdered at least fifty-two women and children between 1978 and 1990 — who was he?
A former dentist turned politician, this founding member of the PTI served as Pakistan's 13th president from 2018 to 2024. Who is he?

Arif Alvi: President of Pakistan from 2018 to 2024. Arif-ur-Rehman Alvi (born 29 July 1949) is a Pakistani politician and former dentist who served as the 13th president of Pakistan from September 2018 to March 2024.
An engineer and inventor who became Indonesia's first vice president to take over mid-term, succeeding Suharto in 1998 and liberalizing the press, who was this third president?
B. J. Habibie: President of Indonesia from 1998 to 1999.
Serving Emperor Justinian I, this Byzantine general reconquered the Vandal Kingdom of North Africa in just nine months and is often called one of the 'Last of the Romans' — who was he?
The only son of a former president and first lady, this Filipino politician was elected vice governor of Ilocos Norte in 1980 before his family was ousted and fled to Hawaii in 1986. Who is he?
Bongbong Marcos: President of the Philippines since 2022.
This Spanish traditionalist political movement backed an alternative Bourbon line descended from Don Carlos, sparking a series of 19th-century civil wars — what's the movement called?
A lawyer who entered politics during the Kaohsiung Incident, he became Taiwan's first president from the DPP in 2000, ending 55 years of Kuomintang rule — who is he?
Chen Shui-bian: President of the Republic of China from 2000 to 2008.

Established by Napoleon after his victory at Austerlitz, this alliance of German client states brought about the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire and lasted until his defeat at Leipzig in 1813 — what was it called?
Confederation of the Rhine: Napoleonic union of German client states.
Born Deedar Randhawa, which Indian wrestler beat Lou Thesz to become world champion in 1968, later playing Hanuman on screen and entering the WWE Hall of Fame?
Dara Singh: Indian professional wrestler and actor (1928–2012)
Holding the title Count of Mordano, this Italian Fascist-era politician also served his country as an ambassador. Who is he?

Ushered in by a decisive 1600 battlefield victory and a shogun title granted by the emperor, this roughly 260-year era of Japanese history brought prolonged peace, strict social order, and a flourishing of arts under isolationist rule — which era is it?
Edo period: Japanese history from 1600 to 1868.
This Austrian chancellor banned the Nazi Party, suppressed the Socialists in the Austrian Civil War, and was assassinated in 1934 during a failed coup by Nazi agents — who was he?
Engelbert Dollfuss: Chancellor of Austria from 1932 to 1934.
Formed in 1980 from four merged Salvadoran guerrilla groups, this left-wing party fought the government throughout a civil war that lasted until 1992 — which group?
Farabundo Martí National Liberation Front: Salvadoran political party and former guerilla organization.
Fired from his Army astronomer post in 1957 during the Lavender Scare, this man turned his dismissal into a landmark fight that helped ignite a more militant gay rights movement. Who was he?
Frank Kameny: American gay rights activist (1925–2011)
Protected around the clock by armed police since 2004, this Dutch politician founded the far-right Party for Freedom and is known for his Euroscepticism and opposition to Islam. Who is he?
This giant Philistine warrior challenged the Israelites to single combat, only to be felled by a young shepherd's sling stone — who is he?
Goliath: Philistine giant in the Bible. According to 1 Samuel, Goliath challenges the Israelites to beat him in single combat.

This successful insurrection by enslaved Africans against French colonial rule in Saint-Domingue climaxed with independence on New Year's Day, 1804, led by the general Toussaint Louverture — what was it called?
Haitian Revolution: 1791–1804 slave revolt in Hispanola.

Said by ancient tradition to have discovered the True Cross during a religious tour of Jerusalem, this Greek-born Augusta was canonized a saint by both the Catholic and Orthodox churches — who was she?
Helena, mother of Constantine I: Roman empress and saint (c. 246–c. 330)
Considered the third person of the Trinity in Nicene Christianity, which concept represents God's animating presence across the Abrahamic faiths?
Holy Spirit: Religious concept with varied meanings.

The son of the labyrinth's architect, this figure from Greek myth escaped imprisonment on wings of feathers and wax, only to plunge into the sea after ignoring his father's warning not to fly too close to the sun — who was he?
Icarus: Greek mythological figure. Icarus and Daedalus escaped using wings Daedalus constructed from birds' molted feathers, threads from blankets, the leather straps from their sandals, and beeswax.
Known informally by the name of the town where it was based, this World War II German puppet state ruled occupied territory from September 1943 until the Axis surrender in 1945 — what was it called?
Italian Social Republic: Puppet state of Nazi Germany (1943–1945)

Married to the sister of North Korea's former supreme leader, this politician was believed to hold de facto power as Kim Jong Il's health failed and rose to vice-chairman of the National Defence Commission — who is he?
A longtime Delaware senator who chaired the Judiciary and Foreign Relations Committees, he served eight years as vice president before reaching the top job himself — who is he?
Joe Biden: President of the United States from 2021 to 2025.
Born in Georgia and rising as a Soviet revolutionary, this figure led from 1924 to 1953 while consolidating power into a dictatorship and codifying Marxism–Leninism — who was he?
Joseph Stalin: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1924 to 1953.

The first woman elected to her union's negotiating team at a plutonium plant, she was found contaminated with plutonium and died in a car crash while driving to meet a New York Times reporter — who was she?
Karen Silkwood: Labor union activist and laboratory technician (1946-1974)
Nicknamed 'the Balkan Prussia' for its frequent wars, this Southeastern European tsardom was proclaimed in 1908 when Prince Ferdinand raised it from a principality — what state was it?
Kingdom of Bulgaria: State in southeastern Europe from 1908 to 1946.
Known to the CIA and Hmong veterans as the 'Secret War,' this Cold War proxy conflict pitted the Communist Pathet Lao against the Royal Lao Government from 1959 to 1975 — what was it?
Laotian Civil War: 1959–1975 conflict in Laos. The Laotian Civil War was waged between the Communist Pathet Lao and the Royal Lao Government from 23 May 1959 to 2 December 1975.
Once considered Chairman Mao's likely successor, this Chinese leader served as president of China from 1959 to 1968 before being purged during the Cultural Revolution — who is he?
Liu Shaoqi: President of China from 1959 to 1968. Liu Shaoqi (Chinese: 刘少奇; pronounced [ljǒʊ ʂâʊtɕʰǐ]; 24 November 1898 – 12 November 1969) was a Chinese revolutionary and politician.
After being ousted as president of Senegal's National Assembly in 2008, this politician founded his own party and went on to defeat his former mentor in the 2012 presidential runoff — who is he?
Macky Sall: President of Senegal from 2012 to 2024.
The last emperor of the Pax Romana, he ruled Rome while also writing as a Stoic philosopher — which of the so-called Five Good Emperors was this?
Marcus Aurelius: Stoic philosopher, Roman emperor from 161 to 180.

Nicknamed 'the Just,' this 15th-century King of Hungary and Croatia was crowned at just fourteen after his brother's execution, and later added the crowns of Bohemia and the title Duke of Austria — who was he?
Matthias Corvinus: King of Hungary and Croatia from 1458 to 1490.
Holding the title 2nd Marquis of Estella, this Spanish military officer ruled as dictator-prime minister from 1923 to 1930 during the twilight of the Bourbon Restoration — who is he?
Miguel Primo de Rivera: Prime Minister of Spain from 1923 to 1930. The coup enjoyed the acquiescence of the monarch, and Primo de Rivera was ensuingly tasked to form a government.

Across Hinduism, Jainism, Buddhism and Sikhism, this term names liberation from the cycle of death and rebirth — in Hindu tradition the highest of life's four aims, beside dharma, artha and kama. What is it?
Moksha: Spiritual liberation in Hinduism, Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism. In its epistemological and psychological senses, moksha requires self-realization, self-actualization, and self-knowledge.
Nephew of a far more famous emperor, he was first elected President of France in 1848, then crowned emperor in 1852, ushering in rapid industrialization — who was he?
Napoleon III: Emperor of the French from 1852 to 1870.
Nicknamed the 'Expressway Man of India' for spearheading projects like the Mumbai-Pune Expressway, this politician has served as Minister of Road Transport since 2014 — who is he?
Dubbed 'the greatest genius the early church ever produced,' which prolific 3rd-century theologian founded a school in Caesarea after starting his career in Alexandria?
Origen: Christian philosopher and theologian (c. 185 – c. 253)

A former primary school teacher and union leader who rose to prominence during a 2017 teachers' strike, this politician served as Peru's president until his failed self-coup in December 2022 — who is he?
Pedro Castillo: President of Peru from 2021 to 2022.
Succeeding John XXIII, this pontiff carried the Second Vatican Council to its 1965 close and built historic bridges with Eastern Orthodox and Protestant churches — who was he?
Pope Paul VI: Head of the Catholic Church from 1963 to 1978.

Employed to paint glow-in-the-dark watch dials in the 1910s and 1920s, these American factory workers were told to point their brushes with their lips — ingesting a radioactive element that would reshape U.S. labor law. Who were they?
Radium Girls: American female radiation poisoning victims (1917–1978)

This political ideology holds that sovereignty belongs to the people and their elected representatives rather than a hereditary monarch, and champions civic virtue, anti-corruption, and freedom from domination — which ideology?
Republicanism: Political ideology centered on citizenship in a state organized as a republic.
Raised in Russian-ruled Poland in a secular Jewish family, this Marxist theorist co-founded the anti-war Spartacus League and is remembered as a champion of socialist democracy — who is she?
This French explorer crossed the Atlantic some two dozen times, drew the first accurate maps of North America's eastern coast and Great Lakes, and founded Quebec City in 1608. Who was he?
Samuel de Champlain: French explorer of North America (1574–1635)

Entering a power-sharing arrangement with his father in 2022, this politician became president after winning 73% of the vote in what's widely considered a sham election, making his nation the first in modern Central Asia ruled by a father-son dynasty — who is he?
Serdar Berdimuhamedow: President of Turkmenistan since 2022.

In 1793, Royalist rebels in this vital French naval port — home to a third of the French fleet — invited a 13,000-strong Anglo-Spanish force to help hold the city against advancing Republican troops — what military engagement was this?
Siege of Toulon (1793): Part of the War of the First Coalition.
A former U.S.-based banker who once backed a rival political party, this businessman scored a surprise win in Syriza's 2023 leadership election before founding his own party — who is he?
Born in Doha in 1980, this man only became heir after an older brother renounced the throne — and he's reigned over his Gulf nation since 2013. Who is he?
Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani: Emir of Qatar since 2013.
At just 33, this Marxist revolutionary became president after a coup staged on his behalf, then launched sweeping reforms he called the people's democratic revolution — who is he?
Thomas Sankara: President of Burkina Faso from 1983 to 1987.
This Indian revolutionary assassinated the former Punjab lieutenant governor in 1940 in revenge for the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre, of which he was a survivor — who was he?
Udham Singh: Indian revolutionary (1899–1940). Singh was subsequently tried and convicted of murder and hanged in July 1940.

Dubbed the 'Merchant of Death' after a 2003 UN report, this former Soviet military translator smuggled weapons from Eastern Europe to Africa and the Middle East before a 2008 Thailand sting — who is he?
One of the most popular presidents at his death in 1923, this Ohio newspaperman who built up the Marion Star saw his reputation later wrecked by exposed scandals — who was he?
Warren G. Harding: President of the United States from 1921 to 1923.
The only Democrat elected president during the Republican-dominated Progressive Era, he steered the U.S. through World War I and championed the League of Nations — which 28th president was he?
Woodrow Wilson: President of the United States from 1913 to 1921.

Rooted mostly among rural Indigenous communities in Chiapas, this Mexican far-left group has been in a frozen conflict with the state since 1994 and takes its name from a revolutionary agrarian commander — which group?
Zapatista Army of National Liberation: Far-left political and militant group in southern Mexico.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henrietta Swan Leavitt (born 1868) is the earliest of the four. Henrietta Swan Leavitt (July 4, 1868 – December 12, 1921) was an American astronomer.

Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Which one below is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Which one below is best known as a chemist?
Wallace Carothers is a chemist. Carothers was a group leader at the DuPont Experimental Station laboratory, near Wilmington, Delaware, where most polymer research was done.
What is the atomic number of Boron?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
In what year was Elon Musk born?
Elon Musk: Elon Reeve Musk (EE-lon; born June 28, 1971) is a businessman and former public official who is the CEO and largest shareholder of Tesla and SpaceX.
In what year was Radium discovered?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
In what year was Copper discovered?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.
Mil Mi-17: Kazan Helicopters. It is known as the Mi-8M series in Russian service.
Which country is Curtiss P-40 Warhawk from?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: United States. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Who is credited with discovering Ruthenium?
Ruthenium: Karl Ernst Claus. Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.
Who is credited with discovering Aniline?
Aniline: Otto Unverdorben. Aniline (From Portuguese: anil, meaning 'indigo shrub', and -ine indicating a derived substance) is an organic compound with the formula C6H5NH2.
Who is credited with discovering Lie group?
Lie group: Sophus Lie. Combining these two ideas, one obtains a continuous group where multiplying points and their inverses is continuous.
With the formula (CH3)2CO, this volatile solvent is produced by the millions of tonnes yearly, much of it to make precursors for plastics like bisphenol A — what is it?
Acetone (2-propanone or dimethyl ketone) is an organic compound with the formula (CH3)2CO.
This genus of more than 650 flowering succulent species includes a 'true' member cultivated worldwide as the standard source for a soothing pharmaceutical gel — what's the genus?
Aloe (also written Alo) is a genus containing over 650 species of flowering succulent plants.

Named in 1835 from the Greek for 'flower' and 'dark blue,' these pH-shifting pigments paint blueberries, black rice, and some autumn leaves anything from red to purple to nearly black — what are they?

Anthocyanin (from Ancient Greek (nthos) 'flower' and / (kuneos/kuanos) 'dark blue'), also called anthocyans, are water-soluble vacuolar pigments that, depending on their pH, may appear red, pink, purple, blue, or black.

Named for the Ancient Greek word for 'star' after its flower shape, this group of roughly 170 mostly Eurasian perennial plants is also known for its late-blooming 'Michaelmas daisies' — which plant group?
Aster (genus) is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the family Asteraceae.
A civil-engineering graduate who first reshaped his father's firm toward real estate, this Frenchman now chairs the world's largest luxury goods company — who is he?
Bernard Arnault (born 5 March 1949) is a French businessman.
This branch of biology studies how plants have grown, reproduced, and evolved over the last 3.5 billion years of life on Earth — what field is it?
Botany is the branch of natural science and biology that studies the growth, reproduction and evolution of plants over the last 3.5 billion years of life on earth.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned what he learned there into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen-food industry. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye (December 9, 1886 - October 7, 1956) was an American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist, who is widely considered the founder of the modern frozen food industry.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.
What unit of time, roughly 24 hours long, marks one full rotation of the Earth relative to the Sun and drives the circadian rhythms of most living things?
Day is the time period of a full rotation of the Earth with respect to the Sun.
Fossils of this Late Devonian armored fish genus, among the earliest vertebrate apex predators ever, have turned up from Morocco to Poland to North America — which genus?
Dunkleosteus is an extinct genus of large arthrodire ("jointed-neck") fish that existed during the Late Devonian period, about 382-358 million years ago.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.
Native to Mediterranean shores, this hardy perennial herb tastes much like anise and lends its flavor to absinthe; one variety swells into a bulb you can eat as a vegetable — what is it?
Fennel (Foeniculum vulgare) is a flowering plant species in the carrot family.
This Canadian physician and author has written five books exploring how childhood trauma shapes conditions from ADHD to addiction, arguing recovery must address underlying emotional pain — who is he?
Gabor Maté (born January 1944) is a Canadian physician and author.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
Tapeworms, flukes, and roundworms burrowing into the gut and beyond all fall under this macroparasitic disease — a neglected tropical illness better known as worm infection. What is it?
Helminthiasis is any macroparasitic disease of humans and other animals in which a part of the body is infected with parasitic worms, known as helminths.
Dissolved in water it yields a notoriously corrosive acid, yet it's also the main industrial route to fluorine and a feedstock for Teflon-style polymers like PTFE — which colorless compound is it?
Hydrogen fluoride is an inorganic compound with chemical formula HF.

Acting as the eye's diaphragm in optical terms, this thin ring-shaped structure controls how much light reaches the retina by adjusting the pupil's size, and also determines a person's eye color — name this structure?

Iris (anatomy) (pl.: irides or irises) is a thin, ring-shaped structure in the eye in most mammals and birds that is responsible for controlling the diameter and size of the pupil, and thus the amount of light reaching the retina.
This Liverpool-born mathematician roamed from finite groups to knot theory, but is best loved for inventing a famous cellular automaton called the Game of Life — who was he?
John Horton Conway (26 December 1937 - 11 April 2020) was an English mathematician.
Named from the Greek word for 'the hidden one', this colorless, odorless noble gas with atomic number 36 is used in fluorescent lamps and high-powered gas lasers. Name the element?
Krypton (from Ancient) is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First isolated from linseed oil and named from the Latin words for 'flax' and 'oil,' this omega-6 polyunsaturated fatty acid is one of the two essential fats humans must get from their diet — which acid?
Linoleic acid (LA) is an organic compound with the formula CH3(CH2)4CH=CHCH2CH=CH(CH2)7COOH.

A chemical element with symbol Mg and atomic number 12, it's a shiny gray metal with low density and high chemical reactivity that readily reacts with air to form a thin passivation oxide coating. What element is this?
Magnesium is a chemical element; it has symbol Mg and atomic number 12. The free metal burns with a brilliant-white light.
First isolated from a cow's pineal gland in 1958 because it could lighten the skin of frogs, this nighttime hormone went on to become famous for governing the sleep-wake cycle — what is it?
Melatonin is a natural compound produced by various organisms, including bacteria and eukaryotes.
This SI base unit for amount of substance, symbol mol, is defined so that one unit contains exactly 6.02214076×10²³ elementary entities — what is it called?
Mole (unit) (symbol mol) is a unit of measurement, the base unit in the International System of Units (SI) for amount of substance.

Which form of alternative medicine, rooted in vitalism and folk healing rather than evidence, gathers 'natural' and 'self-healing' practices ranging from discredited homeopathy to accepted psychotherapy?
Naturopathy is a form of alternative medicine. The ethics of naturopathy have been called into question by medical professionals and its practice has been characterized as quackery.
Despite counting the killer whale and pilot whale among its roughly forty species, this marine mammal family is more closely related to porpoises than to true whales — what family is it?
Oceanic dolphin are a widely distributed family of dolphins that live in the sea.
Located above, below, between, and behind the eyes, these four paired air-filled cavities take their names from the skull bones that contain them — what are they?
Paranasal sinuses are a group of four paired air-filled spaces that surround the nasal cavity.

This insect order's scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek word for 'apparition' or 'phantom' — fitting for a group whose members are famous for disguising themselves as twigs and leaves. What order is this?
Phasmatodea (also known as Phasmida or Phasmatoptera) are an order of insects whose members are variously known as stick insects, stick bugs, walkingsticks, stick animals, or bug sticks.

This large, nearly ubiquitous family of flowering plants provides the world's cereal crops, bamboo, and the plants used in lawns and pastures, ranking as the fifth-largest plant family with roughly 12,000 species — what family is this?
Poaceae (poh-(y)e), also called Gramineae (gr-(y)e), is a large and nearly ubiquitous family of monocotyledonous flowering plants commonly known as true grasses.

This sympathomimetic medication is best known as a nasal decongestant, though at higher doses it can act as a stimulant and appetite suppressant, making it a common drug of abuse — what's the compound called?
Pseudoephedrine is a sympathomimetic medication which is used as a nasal decongestant to treat nasal congestion.
Named from the Latin word for 'net', this light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye functions much like the film or sensor inside a camera. Name this part of the eye?

This zodiac constellation, whose Latin name means 'archer,' is traditionally depicted as a centaur drawing a bow, and its territory in the southern sky contains the center of the Milky Way galaxy. What constellation is this?
Sagittarius (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac and is located in the Southern celestial hemisphere.

Triggered by certain serotonergic medications, this group of symptoms can range from mild high blood pressure to severe, potentially fatal spikes in body temperature and dangerous muscle breakdown — what's it called?
Serotonin syndrome (SS) consists of a group of symptoms that may occur with the use of certain serotonergic medications or drugs.

This genus of about 60 evergreen flowering plant species, native to the tropical Americas and Southeast Asia, is commonly grown as a houseplant valued for its large leaves and elegant white blooms — what genus is it?
Spathiphyllum is a genus of about 60 species of monocotyledonous flowering plants in the family Araceae, native to tropical regions of the Americas and southeastern Asia.
Educated in Rotterdam through World War II, this Indonesian economist later served as minister of finance, trade, and research under two different presidents — who was he?
Sumitro Djojohadikusumo (27 May 1917 - 9 March 2001) was an Indonesian statesman and one of the country's most influential economists.
Used to treat asthma and COPD, this methylxanthine drug — a cousin of caffeine — turns up in trace amounts in tea, chocolate, and yerba mate. What is it?
Theophylline is a drug that inhibits phosphodiesterase and blocks adenosine receptors.
Formed from glycerol bonded to three fatty acids, these molecules make up the main constituents of body fat in humans and are also major components of human skin oil — what are they?
Triglyceride (from tri- and glyceride; also TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids.
This chronic autoimmune disorder strips patches of skin of their pigment, and in antiquity was often wrongly conflated with leprosy — what is it?
Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune disorder that causes patches of skin to lose pigment or color; these vary in size and can appear anywhere on the body.
Almost always found combined with lanthanide minerals and never on its own in nature, this element with symbol Y is a key ingredient in the phosphors used inside LEDs — which element?
Yttrium is a chemical element; it has symbol Y and atomic number 39.

The only legitimate child of the poet Lord Byron, this English mathematician saw that Charles Babbage's analytical engine could do far more than crunch numbers — earning her a reputation as the first computer programmer. Who was she?
Shining as the brightest star in Taurus some 67 light-years from Earth, this red giant has swollen to roughly 45 times the Sun's size despite a cooler surface — which star?
Aldebaran: Taurus Brightest Star. Aldebaran (Arabic: الدَّبَرَان, lit. 'The Follower') is a star in the zodiac constellation of Taurus.
Used to treat dangerous heart rhythms like ventricular fibrillation, which drug can take weeks to work when swallowed but carries risks of lung, liver, thyroid, and eye toxicity?
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Whose name derives from the Sanskrit word 'nimba,' this Mahogany-family tree native to South Asia is the source of a widely used pesticidal oil — which species, and not one of these animals?
Azadirachta indica: Species of plant. Azadirachta indica, commonly known as neem, margosa, nimtree or Indian lilac, is a tree in the Mahogany family Meliaceae.
Named after a barberry-related plant genus and glowing bright yellow under ultraviolet light, this alkaloid was recorded in an ancient Chinese herbal medicine text around 200 BC. What compound is it?
Native to tropical South America, this large non-venomous member of family Boidae is a fixture of private collections thanks to its wildly variable color patterns — what species is it?
Known for a widely viewed 2010 TEDx talk on shame and vulnerability, which academic wrote six consecutive number-one New York Times bestsellers, including Daring Greatly?
Brené Brown: American academic, speaker and author.
This highly soluble white crystalline salt is spread on icy roads for de-icing and, in its anhydrous form, works as a moisture-absorbing desiccant. What compound is it?
Calcium chloride: Chemical compound. The compound is a white crystalline solid at room temperature, and it is highly soluble in water.
Native to the Mediterranean, this legume tree's seed pods are ground into a chocolate substitute, while its seeds yield a common food thickener known as locust bean gum — which tree?
Carob: Small tree grown for its edible pods and landscaping.
This goat-antelope roams mountain ranges from the Pyrenees to the Caucasus and has even been introduced to New Zealand's South Island — which animal?
Named after a 17th-century English physician, this ring-shaped network of arteries supplies blood to the brain in humans and other vertebrates — what is it called?
Circle of Willis: Circulatory anastomosis that supplies blood to the brain and surrounding structures.
In this prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a person cannot be awakened, shows no normal sleep-wake cycle, and may even be induced deliberately during general anesthesia — what is it?
Coma: State of unconsciousness. The person may experience respiratory and circulatory problems due to the body's inability to maintain normal bodily functions.
Going by puma, mountain lion, catamount, and panther depending on where you stand, this big cat is the most widely distributed wild land mammal in the Americas — what is it?
Cougar: Wild cat species native to the Americas.
Native to Mexico and Central America, this tuberous flowering plant blooms in nearly every hue except blue, and its tubers store energy as inulin rather than starch — what is it?
Dahlia: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.

Historically defined by having two embryonic seed leaves, this once-standard division of flowering plants covers around 200,000 species but turned out not to share one common ancestor — which plant group?
Dicotyledon: Historical grouping of flowering plants.
One of the very first vertebrate apex predators on Earth, this armor-plated, jointed-neck fish patrolled open Devonian seas some 380 million years ago — which genus?
This Russian economist served as Vladimir Putin's economic adviser before becoming governor of the Central Bank of Russia — who is she?

Elvira Nabiullina: Russian economist and Governor of the Bank of Russia. Elvira Sakhipzadovna Nabiullina (born 29 October 1963) is a Russian economist and current governor of the Central Bank of Russia.
This branch of anthropology studies individual cultures through participant observation, with roots in early 20th-century social science — what is this field called?
Ethnography: Systematic study of people and cultures.
First described from a skull in 1846 and initially mistaken for a porpoise, this highly social oceanic dolphin gets its common name from a skull resembling that of the orca — which species?
False killer whale: Species of oceanic dolphin in the genus Pseudorca.
Discovered in Dubna in 1999, this superheavy synthetic element (number 114) honors a Russian physicist whose name in Cyrillic explains why its spelling swaps a 'yo' for an 'e' — which element?
Flerovium: Chemical element with atomic number 114 (Fl)

Nicknamed for their nighttime cries, these small nocturnal African primates are, according to the African Wildlife Foundation, the continent's most successful strepsirrhine group — what are they commonly called?
Galago: Family of primates. The Ghanaian name aposor is given to them because of their firm grip on branches.
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Teaching philosophy and astronomy in Roman-era Alexandria, this Neoplatonist is considered the first female mathematician whose life is well documented — who is she?
Sitting on the electromagnetic spectrum between visible light and microwaves, this invisible radiation makes up most of the black-body glow given off by objects near room temperature — what is it?

Infrared: Form of electromagnetic radiation. Infrared (IR; sometimes called infrared light) is electromagnetic radiation (EMR) with wavelengths longer than that of visible light but shorter than microwaves.
Working under Tamerlane around 1400, this Persian astronomer and mathematician produced work that mostly never reached Europe and stays largely unpublished — who is it?
Jamshid al-Kashi: Persian astronomer and mathematician (c. 1380–1429)
Before flying on Space Shuttle mission STS-128 in 2009, this Mexican-American engineer helped develop digital mammography equipment at Lawrence Livermore — who is he?
José M. Hernández: American engineer, vintner, and former NASA astronaut.
Bred for their dazzling colors since the early 19th century in Niigata, Japan, these ornamental carp come in patterns like Kōhaku and Shōwa Sanshoku — what are they?
Koi: Colored varieties of Amur carp.

Native to the dry grasslands and deserts of Afghanistan, Iran, Pakistan, India, and Nepal, this ground-dwelling reptile is so widely captive-bred it's considered the first domesticated species of its kind — what is it?
Leopard gecko: Species of reptile. The leopard gecko is a popular pet, and due to extensive captive breeding it is sometimes referred to as the first domesticated species of lizard.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
Once made by roasting wood — hence its old name 'wood alcohol' — this simplest alcohol smells much like the drinkable kind but is far more poisonous. What is it?

A hemiparasitic plant that taps into its host tree via a structure called the haustorium to steal water and nutrients, its European species was introduced to Northern California in 1900 — what plant is it?
Mistletoe: Common name for various parasitic plants.
Its Inuktitut name means 'the bearded one,' and males emit a strong odor during rut to attract mates — which thick-coated Arctic mammal is this?
Muskox: Species of arctic land mammal.
Popularized by neurologist George Beard in the 1860s, this diagnosis described fatigue, anxiety, and heart palpitations often blamed on the stresses of modern life — what was the condition called?
Grown worldwide as ornamentals in ponds and known to gardeners simply as water lilies, this widespread genus of aquatic plants also includes species considered weeds — which genus?
Nymphaea: Genus of aquatic plants. Nymphaea is a genus of hardy and tender aquatic plants in the family Nymphaeaceae.
This Romanian-American engineer served as Team Principal of the Alpine Formula One team from February 2022 to July 2023 — who is he?
Otmar Szafnauer: American-Romanian engineer, F1 team lead.
Found in mice, cats, birds, humans, and dogs but absent in whales and most reptiles, this triangular bone is the body's largest sesamoid — what is it?
Patella: Kneecap, bone covering knee joint.
Named from the Greek word for 'apparition' due to their leaf-like camouflage, this insect order includes stick insects and leaf insects. What's it called?
Phasmatodea: Order of stick and leaf insects.
Members of this eukaryotic kingdom mostly make their own food with chlorophyll, though parasitic kinds have ditched photosynthesis entirely to feed off others — what kingdom is it?
Plant: Kingdom of organisms. Historically, as in Aristotle's biology, the plant kingdom encompassed all living things that were not animals, and included algae and fungi.
This corticosteroid treats conditions from rheumatoid arthritis to asthma but can cause bone loss and psychiatric side effects with long-term use — what is it called?
Prednisolone: Corticosteroid medication. It can be taken by mouth, injected into a vein, used topically as a skin cream, or as eye drops.
Often starting as a blood clot in the leg that travels to the lungs, this blockage can cause chest pain on breathing in, coughing up blood, and sudden death — what is the condition?

Pulmonary embolism: Blockage of an artery in the lungs. Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a blockage of an artery in the lungs by a substance that has moved from elsewhere in the body through the bloodstream (embolism).

Native to the eastern Himalayas and southwestern China, this small mammal sports dense reddish-brown fur, a ringed tail, and curved semi-retractile claws for climbing — and was the original bearer of its famous name. What is it?
Red panda: Species of mammal in Asia.
First created in 1994 near Darmstadt, Germany, this extremely radioactive synthetic element is named for the physicist who discovered X-rays — which element is it?
Roentgenium: Chemical element with atomic number 111 (Rg)
Also called elder or elderberry, this tree or shrub's flowers and berries are traditionally used to make cordial and wine — what's its scientific name?
Sambucus nigra: Species of flowering plant in the moschatel family.
The sole living species in its genus, this coastal California evergreen is the tallest tree species on Earth, reaching over 116 meters and living 2,200 years or more. What is it?
Sequoia sempervirens: Species of tree. Sequoia sempervirens is the sole living species of the genus Sequoia in the cypress family Cupressaceae (formerly treated in Taxodiaceae).

Its last natural case appeared in 1977, and in 1980 the WHO declared it the only human disease ever wiped off the Earth — which scourge, known for fluid-filled blisters that scarred survivors, was it?
It's the largest order of reptiles — lizards and snakes alike — set apart by horny scales they periodically shed and a hinged upper jaw that lets snakes gape around big prey. Which order?
Squamata: Order of reptiles. The now-extinct mosasaurs reached lengths over 14 m (46 ft).
Starting his career as a materials engineer and later overseeing the launch of Chrome and Google Drive, who has served as CEO of both Google and its parent company since 2015 and 2019 respectively?
Sundar Pichai: CEO of Alphabet Inc. and Google (born 1972)
Feigning injury or authority to lure victims to his car, this American serial killer murdered young women across five states in the mid-1970s before revisiting their graves. Who was he?
Known commonly as garden thyme or German thyme, this flowering plant belongs to the mint family — which species is it?
Thymus vulgaris: Species of flowering plant.
This condition involves a long-term urge to pull out one's own hair, most often from the scalp or around the eyes, and is more common among those with OCD — what is it?
Formed by the fusion of membrane vesicles, this shapeless organelle in plant and fungal cells is basically a water-filled storage sac that can even hold engulfed solids. What is it?
Vacuole: Membrane-bound organelle in cells containing fluid.
Descended from a wild bovine ancestor, this large domesticated animal from the Indian subcontinent now also grazes fields in Italy, the Balkans, and Australia — what is it?
Water buffalo: Species of large bovine. The wild water buffalo (Bubalus arnee) is most probably the ancestor of the domestic water buffalo.
Making up only about 1% of described fungal species, this single-celled organism reproduces by budding or fission and is so tiny it usually measures just 3 to 4 micrometres across — what is it?
The symbol for argon is Ar. Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
What is the chemical symbol for cadmium?
The symbol for cadmium is Cd. Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.

In what year was Jack Quaid born?
Jack Quaid: Jack Henry Quaid (born April 24, 1992) is an American actor.
In what year was Patrick Stewart born?
Patrick Stewart: Sir Patrick Stewart (born 13 July 1940) is an English actor.
In what year was Stan Lee born?
Stan Lee (born Stanley Martin Lieber; December 28, 1922 – November 12, 2018) was an American comic book writer, editor, publisher, and producer.
In what year was Joe Pesci born?
Joe Pesci: Joseph Frank Pesci (Italian: [ˈpeʃʃi]; born February 9, 1943) is an American actor and singer.
In what year was Jayne Mansfield born?
Jayne Mansfield (born Vera Jayne Palmer; April 19, 1933 – June 29, 1967) was an American actress, Playboy Playmate, and singer.
In what year was Diane Lane born?
Diane Lane (born January 22, 1965) is an American actress.
